title: EIP-8279: Block Access List Byte Floor
description: Meter EIP-7928 Block Access List bytes at runtime and fold them into the EIP-7623 transaction floor, capping worst-case block size.
author: Toni Wahrstätter (@nerolation)
laymanDescription: Ethereum charges a minimum price per byte a transaction adds to a block, so a cheap block can never be an enormous one. Block access lists are a new source of bytes that nothing prices, letting an attacker inflate a block to 1.55 MB using cold storage reads. This proposal meters them at the same rate.
benefits: Caps worst-case block content near 0.89 MB, roughly 42% below the current 1.55 MB
Closes the calldata plus cold-SLOAD bypass that EIP-8131 alone leaves open
One flat per-byte rate, so the worst case no longer depends on the attacker's choice
tradeoffs: Adds 0.54 pp more transactions paying more and 0.77 pp more gas, on top of EIP-8131
Wallets and eth_estimateGas must simulate runtime metering, not just intrinsic gas
The meter deliberately over-counts, never rewinding bytes charged in reverted frames
